prompt: Describe Ryanair's (or another low-cost airline's) business model with the three components value creation, value configuration and value capture.
modelAnswer: Value creation: cheap point-to-point flights for price-sensitive leisure and business travellers who value price over comfort. Value configuration: one aircraft type (lower maintenance and training costs), high aircraft utilization and fast turnarounds, secondary airports with low fees, direct online sales, no free extras, standardized processes. Value capture: margin from very low costs per seat plus ancillary revenues (luggage, seat choice, priority boarding, partner offers) – low base fares fill planes, extras and cost discipline generate the margin.
keyPoints: Configuration of activities consistent with low cost

prompt: Explain the risk of being “stuck in the middle” and under which conditions a firm can combine cost leadership and differentiation.
modelAnswer: Porter's generic strategies require a clear choice between lower costs and higher perceived value, because they call for different activities, structures and cultures (centralized, specialized, operations-driven vs flexible, marketing- and R&D-driven). A firm that tries to do both risks having neither the lowest cost nor the highest value and ends up with poor performance (JCPenney vs Walmart and Macy's). Combining both is possible when activities are compartmentalized (different units for different positions) or when value innovation creates a new market space where the firm eliminates and reduces costly factors while raising and creating valued ones (blue ocean, e.g. CitizenM, Nintendo Wii) – such dual advantage is usually limited in time.

prompt: A premium chocolate maker considers selling a low-priced line in supermarkets to boost growth. Discuss the move with the generic strategies framework.
modelAnswer: Today the firm pursues (focused) differentiation: high quality, brand, premium price, selective channels. A low-priced supermarket line moves towards cost leadership in a broad market, where it competes with players having scale and input-cost advantages. Risks: stuck in the middle (not cheap enough vs mass brands, brand dilution vs premium rivals), cannibalization of the premium line, conflicts in the value chain (sourcing, production standards, sales force). Conditions for success: compartmentalize the activities (separate brand, separate production and sourcing) or create a genuinely new value curve. Otherwise growth comes better from deepening the differentiation position (new premium segments, geographies).
keyPoints: New line implies cost logic and broader scope
Stuck in the middle / brand dilution / cannibalization
Conditions: compartmentalization or deepening the position
